name: CLIPER (CLIP-based Facial Expression Recognition with Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning)
authors_or_creators: Hanting Li, Hongjing Niu, Zhaoqing Zhu, Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China, USTC)
publication_venue: arXiv preprint (2023); subsequently presented at ICME 2024 [uncertain]
backbone: CLIP ViT-B/16 image encoder + CLIP Transformer text encoder (frozen, with learnable prompts)
param_count: ~150 (CLIP ViT-B/16 + text encoder); only a small number of prompt tokens are trainable in the parameter-efficient stage [uncertain]
accuracy_affectnet: 61.98% on AffectNet-7 class and ~57-58% on AffectNet-8 class (Overall accuracy reported in the paper) [uncertain]
accuracy_rafdb: 91.61% Overall accuracy on RAF-DB basic 7-class subset [uncertain]
hardware_requirements: Training on a single NVIDIA RTX 3090 / V100-class GPU is sufficient due to parameter-efficient prompt tuning (only prompt tokens updated); inference uses standard CLIP ViT-B/16 footprint [uncertain]
loss_function: Cross-entropy classification loss over similarity scores between image features and class-specific text-prompt embeddings; two-stage training with multi-modal prompt learning (coarse-grained then fine-grained class-aware prompts)
pretraining_strategy: VLM-pretrain (initialized from CLIP pretrained on 400M image-text pairs); FER adaptation uses parameter-efficient prompt tuning rather than full fine-tuning
pretraining_corpus: WIT (WebImageText, ~400M image-text pairs collected by OpenAI for CLIP)
robustness: Parameter-efficient prompt tuning is argued to preserve CLIP's robust pretrained representations and reduce overfitting to small FER datasets; explicit Occlusion-RAF-DB / Pose-RAF-DB numbers not reported [uncertain]
explainability: Class-aware text prompts provide semantic interpretability of the decision (which textual concept best matches the image); CLIP attention maps can be visualized
